clue.text: Casual interest in undemanding sort of fabric

parts.note: casual means relaxed or easy
to have an interest in something is to care about it

explanation.surface: Someone shows only a passing interest in a low-maintenance textile.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric labelled this needs little attention when washed, so it is an undemanding material to look after.

clue.text: Rubbing noses is OK with me, anyway

definitions.text: Rubbing noses is OK with me, anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to rub noses as a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubbing noses is popularly called an Eskimo kiss; the whole clue both defines and builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose-rubbing as a greeting is popularly associated with Arctic peoples of Greenland and Canada.

clue.text: Earth colour as in NE, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A query about whether a colour of soil is like the one in the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: This brownish pigment is made from natural earth from Tuscany.

clue.text: Sort of square piece of luggage outside station in India

indicators.note: outside means one word is placed around another

parts.note: a case is a suitcase
a T-square is a sort of square

explanation.surface: A square suitcase is left outside an Indian railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' here means social rank, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: In India, hereditary social class determines a person's rank or position in society.

clue.text: Bribe for dissolute fellow, not working?

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A bribe offered to an idle libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit share of profits taken by someone is a kind of bribe.

clue.text: A paddle on the surface of the water?

definitions.text: on the surface of the water

parts.note: a float is one of the paddles or boards on a paddle wheel or waterwheel

explanation.surface: A question about whether a paddle rests on top of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floating rather than sinking is buoyed up on the top of the water.

clue.text: No charge at west end of coast

parts.note: free means costing nothing
the heel is the end of a loaf

explanation.surface: Free admission at the western tip of a coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' is a verb here: to move without power.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast on a bicycle is to travel without pedalling.

clue.text: No silly men here, in the deep?

definitions.text: No silly men here, in the deep?

parts.words: No silly men here, in the deep?
parts.note: in cricket, silly positions are close to the batsman, while the deep is the far part of the field

explanation.surface: A sea where there are no foolish people.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'silly' mid-on and similar fielders stand very close to the batsman; 'the deep' is the far boundary area.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a cricket field far from the batsman holds the deep fielders, never the silly ones.

clue.text: One may carry a drop when greeting in Scotland

definitions.text: One may carry a drop when greeting in Scotland

parts.words: One may carry a drop when greeting in Scotland
parts.note: in Scots, to greet means to weep, so the reading is a duct carrying a tear

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink along when saying hello in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is Scots for weep; the drop is a tear, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The small channel draining fluid from the eye carries teardrops when one weeps.

clue.text: Retain rice-wine as a memento

parts.note: to retain something is to keep it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a bottle of Japanese wine as a souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir kept to remind one of a person or event.

clue.text: Out-of-breath girl

indicators.note: out of order or shape tells us the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl left panting after running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-breath' looks like one description of the girl, but 'Out-of' signals an anagram of BREATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a girl's name.

clue.text: Small strikes in sympathy?

parts.note: reads like sympathy industrial action, but means light taps given as comfort

explanation.surface: Minor industrial walkouts in support of other workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Light taps given to comfort someone are small blows in sympathy.

clue.text: Nominates wrong state

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are set out incorrectly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party puts forward the wrong candidate for a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Bizarre low dam needs a key

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: A strange little dam on a river apparently requires a key to work it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and strange are synonyms for something uncanny or odd.

clue.text: Cook-champion given keys

parts.note: E is a musical key
F is another musical key

explanation.surface: A prize-winning cook is presented with keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cook in a restaurant kitchen is called by this French title.

clue.text: Apartheid smashed in celebration of popular songs

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People celebrate with popular songs after apartheid is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart ranking the best-selling records is a showcase of popular songs.

clue.text: She will lead Bill in a record finish

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, so the first pair of words comes before the next

parts.note: she will contracts to she'll, giving these letters
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman will head a bill in a record-breaking finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Shellac is both a varnish (finish) and the material of old 78rpm records.
explanation.definitionFit: This resin was used for gramophone discs and is also a wood varnish, so it is a record material and a finish.

clue.text: Ship's light?

parts.note: reads as a lamp on a vessel, but means a window letting light into it

explanation.definitionFit: A round window in a vessel's side lets in light.

clue.text: Plead with Barnaby to be stingy

parts.note: to plead is to beg
Barnaby Rudge is a Dickens novel and its title character

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a man called Barnaby not to be mean.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is a novel by Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something grudgingly or resent giving it is to be ungenerous.

clue.text: Surpass in public work

parts.note: overt means open, public
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone tries to outdo others in public works.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or exceed, as a river overtops its banks.

clue.text: Inner part of mine hot?

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A question about whether the interior of a mine is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft core of a plant stem or the essence of something is its inner part.

clue.text: Bar limit?

definitions.meaning: an extreme point, as at the end of the earth's axis

explanation.definitionFit: A pole is a long rod, and also either extremity of the earth, its limit.

clue.text: Prattle about Chaucer's hen

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chatter about a hen in Chaucer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pertelote, the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, is called by this name in later English.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Partlet is the traditional name for a hen, from the hen in Chaucer's tale.

clue.text: Songster allowed outside pub

indicators.note: outside means one word is placed around another

parts.note: to let is to allow
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A singer is permitted outside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: This small finch is noted for its singing, so it is a songbird.

clue.text: Excited lad clutches half-sovereign of ancient date

indicators.note: clutches means holds inside, so one piece goes within another
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sovereign can be King George; half of that name gives these letters

explanation.surface: An excited boy grips an old ten-shilling coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges LAD to ALD, which 'clutches' GEO, half of GEORGE (a sovereign, or king).
explanation.definitionFit: Something dating from long ago has existed for ages, so it is very old.

clue.text: Roman ground seen in Chester racecourse?

indicators.note: seen in tells us the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: A Roman site turns up at an old city racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is a Roman city in north-west England with a famous racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin, the language of the Romans, the word for earth or land is this.

clue.text: Article about ill-advised punishment

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, one word placed around another

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
a rash act is ill-advised

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a foolish penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating is a form of punishment.

clue.text: Divers around middle of French river

indicators.note: around means surrounding, one piece placed about another

parts.note: divers means several, some
M is an abbreviation for middle

explanation.surface: Divers swim around the middle of a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is an old word for various, not people swimming underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme flows through northern France to the English Channel.

clue.text: Test of yellow gold bargain?

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry, shown as yellow
a deal is a bargain

explanation.surface: A trial of whether yellow gold is good value.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial by fire or water was an old way of testing guilt; a harrowing experience is a severe test.

clue.text: Passionate music of ladylove with sergeant, perhaps

parts.note: an old flame is a sweetheart
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A soldier and his beloved inspire heated music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish gypsy style of song and dance is known for its fiery intensity.

clue.text: Team to appear one by one

definitions.meaning: the numeral written as figures looks like a 1 next to a 1

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has this many players, and in figures it is two ones side by side.

clue.text: Watching first-class cricket match, chap declared

parts.note: watching a match is being at it
a Test is an international first-class cricket match
Ed is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man watching a Test match makes an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international cricket match lasting several days.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or certify formally as true.
